findings.text: The node's headline property - every batch item gets a comparator share - holds only for batch lengths up to 30, and production configures a batch length of 50. VERDICT: not MUST-FIX (the arithmetic forbids the alternative while the cap stays 30), but the limit is undocumented and untested. Concrete triggering input: an ExtractionBatch of 31 items each returning five unique search results. per_item_allowance = max(1, 30 // 31) = 1, the first 30 items each take their one, and the 31st (index 30) hits 'if len(nearby) >= cap: break' on its first result and contributes zero. Measured items-with-zero-comparators: n=30 gives 0, n=31 gives 1, n=32 gives 2, n=200 gives 170. This is reachable, not hypothetical: pyproject sets name-only-batch-size = 50 and group_for_name_only (imas_codex/standard_names/enrichment.py:800) chunks group_items at exactly that size, so a dense name-only bin is a 50-item batch in which 20 items still contribute nothing - the same starvation this node fixed, at one fifth the severity and in one mode only. The named batch size at which the floor of one makes the first pass alone exceed the cap is 31. WOULD THE NODE'S OWN TEST CATCH IT: no. Both fixtures build range(25), where 30 // 25 = 1 satisfies every item and the property is simply true. The repair is either a docstring sentence naming 30 as the batch length above which the share degrades to the first thirty items, or a names-mode cap that scales with the batch.

The per-item floor is enforced by statement order, not by the max(1, ...) that appears to enforce it. VERDICT: SOUND today, a latent durability defect. Replacing per_item_allowance = max(1, cap // len(items)) with the bare cap // len(items) yields byte-identical results - same total, same contributor count, same id order - at n = 1, 5, 25, 30, 31, 40, 50 and 200, because the 'added >= per_item_allowance' test runs AFTER the append, so an allowance of 0 still admits the first result of each item. The max() therefore fires only when len(items) > cap, which is exactly the regime where the cap guard makes it irrelevant. Concrete triggering input for the latent defect: move the allowance test above the append (a plausible tidy-up, since the two cap checks then read together) and every batch longer than 30 loses its floor entirely while both landed tests stay green. WOULD THE NODE'S OWN TEST CATCH IT: no, neither the removal nor the reorder, because at n=25 the allowance is 1 under every variant. One assertion at n=31 pins the real mechanism.

Efficiency, on the compose hot path. The helper materialises results_by_item eagerly - one _search_nearby_names call per item, completing before any allocation - where the removed loop stopped searching once the cap filled. Measured for identical inputs: 6 searches before versus 25 after at the default batch-size 25 (4.2x), and 6 versus 50 at name-only-batch-size 50 (8.3x). Each call reaches search_standard_names_vector against the live graph, and all of them are synchronous calls inside the async _compose_batch_body (workers.py:3790) with no await and no asyncio.to_thread, so they serialise on the event loop against the configured compose concurrency. Most of the increase is the necessary price of the fix. The waste is specific: for a batch longer than 30, items 31 onward receive no first-pass allowance and the refill pass only runs under 'if len(nearby) < cap', so in a full 50-item name-only bin roughly 20 of the 50 searches cannot affect the output at all. Concrete triggering input: any 50-item name-only batch whose first 30 items each return one unique result - the cap fills in the first pass and 20 vector searches were paid for nothing. WOULD THE NODE'S OWN TEST CATCH IT: no - the injected stub search is free, and test_every_item_receives_a_comparator_before_budget_refill actually ASSERTS the eager behaviour (searched == every item's description), so the cost is pinned in rather than flagged. Bounding the eager pass at cap items keeps the fix and drops the waste.

Coverage gap rather than a defect, and it is the gate's third question. Neither test exercises either call site: both invoke the helper directly with an injected search, so the two lines the extraction exists for - _collect_nearby_name_comparators(batch.items) at workers.py:3790 and _collect_nearby_name_comparators(batch) at workers.py:5654 - are unpinned by the whole suite. Concrete triggering input: swap them. Passing a bare ExtractionBatch at site one makes the helper iterate a dataclass and raise TypeError at compose time; passing batch.items at site two raises AttributeError on a list. Both are green under the focused gate, the negative control and the full tests/standard_names run. I verified both sites correct by reading the annotations (ExtractionBatch.items is list[dict] at sources/base.py:188; compose_batch's batch is list[dict] at workers.py:5518), which is reading, not a demonstrated control. WOULD THE NODE'S OWN TEST CATCH IT: no. Also unconstructed: any batch length other than 25, so n=1, n=30, n=31 and n=200 - the sizes the fence names - are all unmeasured by the node.

Recorded as a positive so it is not re-derived, and it answers the second half of the gate's first question with a demonstration. The cap guard is not merely asserted, it is held by a test: dropping the second pass's PRE-append 'if len(nearby) >= cap: break' and keeping only the post-append one lets the total reach 52 comparators at n=25 and 35 at n=7, and test_item_without_search_results_uses_no_comparator_share turns RED on it (assertion 52 != 30). Worth knowing before either test is edited: test_every_item_receives_a_comparator_before_budget_refill stays GREEN on that same mutation, because its shared_comparator id absorbs enough duplicates to land the total back on 30 - so of the two tests exactly one defends the bound, and it is the one whose name is about an empty search result. A 3000-trial fuzz over random batch sizes 1..60 with duplicate-heavy random id pools reached a maximum total of exactly 30 and leaked zero duplicate ids, so the landed second pass cannot exceed the cap.

justifications.durability: The guard that matters is genuinely pinned, and I demonstrated it rather than inferring it - but only at one batch size, and the expression that appears to enforce the per-item floor does not. WHAT IS DEFENDED: mutating the second pass to drop its pre-append cap guard (keeping only the post-append one) lets the total run to 52 comparators at n=25 and 35 at n=7, and test_item_without_search_results_uses_no_comparator_share turns RED on it. So the cap is not merely asserted, it is held by a test. Notably test_every_item_receives_a_comparator_before_budget_refill stays GREEN on that same mutation, because its shared_comparator id makes the arithmetic land back on 30 - so the cap is defended by one of the two tests, not both, which is worth knowing before either is edited. DOCKED FOR THREE REACHABLE GAPS THE LANDED TESTS DO NOT CONSTRUCT. First, THE max(1, ...) FLOOR IS DECORATIVE AND NOTHING NOTICES. Replacing per_item_allowance = max(1, cap // len(items)) with the bare cap // len(items) produces byte-identical output at n=1, 5, 25, 30, 31, 40, 50 and 200 - same totals, same contributor counts, same id order. The floor is actually enforced by STATEMENT ORDER: the allowance test 'added >= per_item_allowance' runs AFTER the append, so an allowance of 0 still admits one result per item. That is fine today, but it means the line a later reader will trust is not the line doing the work, and reordering the append below the allowance test would silently starve every batch larger than 30 while both tests stayed green. One test at n=31 asserting the 31st item's treatment would pin the real mechanism. Second, NO BATCH SIZE OTHER THAN 25 IS EVER CONSTRUCTED. Both fixtures build range(25). The regime the fence asks about - and the regime production reaches through name-only-batch-size = 50 - is entirely unpinned: a change that broke n=1 (total 5) or n=50 (total 30, first 30 items only) would pass every gate in this node. Third, NEITHER TEST EXERCISES EITHER CALL SITE. Both call the helper directly, so if site one had been written _collect_nearby_name_comparators(batch) against an ExtractionBatch - iterating the dataclass, which raises - or site two had been written batch.items against a list, the focused gate, the negative control and the full tests/standard_names run would all still be green. Those two lines are the whole point of the extraction and no test touches them.
justifications.evidence: Strong, and every cited log was opened and matches. THE DEFECT REPRODUCTION IS REAL AND I REPRODUCED IT INDEPENDENTLY. defect-reproduction.log records {batch_items: 25, items_with_results: 25, contributing_items: 6, total_comparators: 30, contributor_indices: [0,1,2,3,4,5]}. Re-implementing the removed inline loop verbatim from the diff and running it in this reviewer's worktree gives the same figures - 30 comparators from 6 of 25 contributing items, contributors exactly the first six - and the same instrument shows the landed helper giving 30 comparators from 25 of 25. So the measure the fence names is confirmed from the landed diff and not taken from the report. THE NEGATIVE CONTROL IS WELL FORMED. Its first line repeats the declared mutation verbatim - 'negative_control mutation: set the per-item allowance to the full five-result search width, recreating first-six budget exhaustion' - exit_status 1, and it names both failing tests with their failing assertions quoted. It is the right mutation: it restores exactly the starvation the change exists to remove. THE SUITE DELTA CHECKS ARITHMETICALLY AND I RECOMPUTED THE IDS MYSELF. Baseline at 9c93e6a0e ends '22 failed, 7507 passed, 8 skipped, 326 deselected, 34 warnings, 3 errors' exit 1; after at b08547968 ends '20 failed, 7511 passed, 8 skipped, 326 deselected, 34 warnings, 3 errors' exit 1. 22+7507 = 7529 and 20+7511 = 7531 = 7529 + the 2 tests added, so the collection accounts for exactly the new file. Extracting the terminal ids from both logs and diffing them: ADDED FAILURES = 0, and the two REMOVED are precisely the two the manifest names, test_refine_model_dispatch::test_refine_docs_worker_imports_refine_section and ::test_refine_name_worker_imports_refine_section, which the manifest correctly reports as baseline-only and outside this node's reach. The focused gate re-run here at the integrated head returns 2 passed exit 0 (review-node-test.log). One instrument correction worth recording so it is not re-derived: my first id extraction counted 26 baseline and 24 after against the manifest's 25 and 23; the extra line is an application DEBUG line beginning 'ERROR imas_codex.standard_names.export:' rather than a test id, so the manifest's counts are the correct ones and my grep was the thing at fault. DOCKED TWICE, both for evidence that was available and not taken. First, NO BOUNDARY IS MEASURED ANYWHERE. Both test fixtures and the reproduction all use a 25-item batch; nothing in the node's evidence touches n=1, n=30, n=31 or n=200, which is where the cap arithmetic and the per-item floor actually interact, and which the fence asks about by name. I produced those figures here in one short probe, so the cost was low. Second, NO LOG EXERCISES EITHER CALL SITE. Both tests call the helper directly with an injected search, so the third fenced question - whether batch.items and batch are the right containers - is answered in this review by reading the two type annotations, and by nothing the node ran.
justifications.fit: The extraction is the right move and reads like the module. Two identical fifteen-line inline loops become one documented helper whose docstring states the mechanism (first pass shares, second pass refills, dedup by standard-name id) rather than the plan item; cap and per_item_k become keyword defaults carrying the former _NEARBY_CAP and _PER_ITEM_K values so the prompt bound is unchanged; the search seam is a Callable[..., list[dict]] | None defaulting to the real function, which is a clean injection point and is what let this review measure anything at all. The defect removed is precisely the outer 'if len(nearby) >= _NEARBY_CAP: break', and because the new first pass has no outer break, results_by_item and next_result_indices are always the same length, which is what makes the strict=True zip in the refill pass safe rather than optimistic. DOCKED THREE TIMES. First, the decorative max(1, ...) covered under durability - an expression that states an invariant it does not enforce. Second, and the larger one, THE HELPER NOW ISSUES ONE VECTOR SEARCH PER ITEM EAGERLY, in a list comprehension that completes before any allocation happens. Measured search-call counts for the same inputs: at the default batch-size 25 the removed loop issued 6 and the helper issues 25 (4.2x); at name-only-batch-size 50 the removed loop issued 6 and the helper issues 50 (8.3x). These are calls to _search_nearby_names, which reaches search_standard_names_vector against the live graph, and they are synchronous calls made from inside the async _compose_batch_body with no await and no asyncio.to_thread, so they serialise on the event loop against whatever compose concurrency is configured. Some of this increase is the price of the fix and is correct - you cannot give every item a share without asking every item. But for a batch longer than 30 the searches for items 31 onward buy nothing in the common case, because those items get no first-pass allowance and the refill pass only runs when 'len(nearby) < cap' - so roughly 20 of the 50 searches in a full name-only bin are wasted work on the hot path. Bounding the eager pass at cap items, or spending the budget lazily, would keep the fix and drop the cost. Third, a smaller asymmetry: the refill pass has no outer break, so once the cap fills it keeps iterating the remaining items' slices doing nothing. Cheap, but this change exists because an outer break was in the wrong place, so leaving the mirrored loop without one reads as accidental rather than chosen.
justifications.goal_fidelity: VERDICT SOUND, with one bounded limitation that is arithmetic rather than a coding defect. Read from the landed diff at the integrated head, not the worker's report: both node commits are ancestors of HEAD 10d2725c0 (git merge-base --is-ancestor returns 0 for b08547968 and 172be6de7), and the marker the change INTRODUCED is present there - git show HEAD:imas_codex/standard_names/workers.py | grep -n _collect_nearby_name_comparators returns the definition at 1803 and both call sites at 3790 and 5654. THE FOUR FENCED QUESTIONS, each answered with a measurement taken in this reviewer's worktree (review-allocation-probe.log). (1) IS THE TOTAL STILL BOUNDED BY 30 FOR EVERY BATCH SIZE, AND CAN THE SECOND PASS EXCEED IT - YES bounded, NO the second pass cannot exceed. Measured totals: n=1 gives 5, n=5 gives 25, n=25 gives 30, n=29 gives 30, n=30 gives 30, n=31 gives 30, n=50 gives 30, n=200 gives 30. The reason is structural: every append in both passes is preceded by an 'if len(nearby) >= cap: break' evaluated at the top of the inner iteration, so an append can only occur while len(nearby) < cap and the list can therefore reach cap but never pass it. Demonstrated rather than asserted with a 3000-trial fuzz over random batch sizes 1..60 and duplicate-heavy random id pools: maximum total observed 30, and zero duplicate ids leaked in any trial. (2) DOES EVERY ITEM WITH AT LEAST ONE SEARCH RESULT NOW CONTRIBUTE AT LEAST ONE COMPARATOR, AND NAME THE BATCH SIZE AT WHICH THE FLOOR OF ONE MAKES THE FIRST PASS ALONE EXCEED THE CAP - YES for every batch length up to and including 30, NO above it, and the batch size is 31. At 31 the floor of one demands 31 comparators against a cap of 30, so the first pass alone would have to exceed the cap; the cap guard wins and the 31st item (index 30) contributes zero. Measured items-with-zero-comparators against a search returning five unique results per item: n=30 gives 0, n=31 gives 1 (index 30), n=32 gives 2, n=200 gives 170. This matters in production and not only in theory: pyproject sets batch-size = 25 for default compose, where the fix is complete (contributors 6/25 before, 25/25 after), but name-only-batch-size = 50, and group_for_name_only (enrichment.py:800) chunks at exactly that size, so a maximally dense name-only bin is a 50-item ExtractionBatch in which 20 items still contribute nothing. Raised as a finding and a docs/test gap, not as MUST-FIX, because giving 50 items a share of 30 is not arithmetically possible while the cap stays at 30 - the honest repair is to say so, or to raise the cap for names mode. (3) ARE THE TWO CALL SITES PASSING THE SAME THING, AND IS THAT CORRECT AT BOTH - YES both are correct, and the asymmetry is required rather than a slip. Site one (workers.py:3790, inside _compose_batch_body) passes batch.items where batch is an ExtractionBatch; ExtractionBatch is a dataclass whose items field is annotated list[dict] (sources/base.py:188), so iteration yields the item dicts. Site two (workers.py:5654, inside compose_batch) passes batch directly, and compose_batch's own signature is batch: list[dict] (workers.py:5518) with a docstring describing 'a list of pre-claimed items (dicts with path, description, physics_domain)'. Neither container yields anything other than the item dicts the helper reads description and path from, and both match the containers the two inline loops iterated before the change - site one iterated batch.items, site two iterated batch. (4) DOES THE HELPER'S SEARCH CALL PRESERVE THE PER-ITEM QUERY - YES, unchanged. The helper passes item.get('description') or item.get('path', '') with k=per_item_k defaulting to 5, character-for-character the hint expression both inline loops used with their _PER_ITEM_K = 5. Executed here against three items - one with a description, one with only a path, one with an empty-string description - the recorded queries are ['D', 'c/d', 'e/f'], so the falsy-description fallback to path still fires.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat 9c93e6a0e..172be6de7 is 4 files and exactly the 4 declared write paths, nothing else: imas_codex/standard_names/workers.py (+102/-36), tests/standard_names/test_comparator_budget_share.py (+50, new), docs/evidence/archive/sn-lifecycle-integrity-landed.html (+40) and docs/plans/sn-lifecycle-integrity.html (+3). The plan edit is a 3-line worker-owned landing record; no plan version, modified date, followup status or terminal state is touched, which the manifest states and the diff size confirms. Both commits are conventional with real bodies - 'fix(standard-names): share nearby comparator capacity' and 'docs(evidence): record comparator allocation result' - and a case-insensitive scan of both messages for co-authored-by / generated with / claude / copilot returns 0 hits. Naming is clean: the extracted symbol is _collect_nearby_name_comparators and the new file is test_comparator_budget_share.py, both mechanism names carrying no plan, sprint, phase or ticket label, and the added comments describe the bound rather than the plan item. Both commits are ancestors of the integrated head. The out-of-scope failures the node met - the two test_refine_model_dispatch cases in a module this change cannot reach - are reported under follow_ons and left untouched, which is the correct disposition. No stray file, no generated model staged, no second environment created.

The defect removed is precisely the outer 'if len(nearby) >= _NEARBY_CAP: break', and because the new first pass has no outer break, results_by_item and next_result_indices are always the same length, which is what makes the strict=True zip in the refill pass safe rather than optimistic. DOCKED THREE TIMES. First, the decorative max(1, ...) covered under durability - an expression that states an invariant it does not enforce. Second, and the larger one, THE HELPER NOW ISSUES ONE VECTOR SEARCH PER ITEM EAGERLY, in a list comprehension that completes before any allocation happens. Measured search-call counts for the same inputs: at the default batch-size 25 the removed loop issued 6 and the helper issues 25 (4.2x); at name-only-batch-size 50 the removed loop issued 6 and the helper issues 50 (8.3x). These are calls to _search_nearby_names, which reaches search_standard_names_vector against the live graph, and they are synchronous calls made from inside the async _compose_batch_body with no await and no asyncio.to_thread, so they serialise on the event loop against whatever compose concurrency is configured. Some of this increase is the price of the fix and is correct - you cannot give every item a share without asking every item. But for a batch longer than 30 the searches for items 31 onward buy nothing in the common case, because those items get no first-pass allowance and the refill pass only runs when 'len(nearby) < cap' - so roughly 20 of the 50 searches in a full name-only bin are wasted work on the hot path. Bounding the eager pass at cap items, or spending the budget lazily, would keep the fix and drop the cost. Third, a smaller asymmetry: the refill pass has no outer break, so once the cap fills it keeps iterating the remaining items' slices doing nothing. Cheap, but this change exists because an outer break was in the wrong place, so leaving the mirrored loop without one reads as accidental rather than chosen.
